alternatives.concept: Study sustainable innovation through institutions, economic incentives, public policy, business strategy and behavioural change, joined to spatial engineering, geospatial analysis, nature-based infrastructure and water adaptation. Environmental assessment and mixed research connect these strands into a related socio-technical response to the displayed Urban Planning and Mobility basis. This does not reproduce its full transport, land-use, smart-city engineering or compulsory final-project formation.

alternatives.concept: A related sustainable-energy and environmental-systems direction supported by the programme’s available Sustainable Energy specialization: climate science, renewable-system design, resources, water, environmental chemistry, circularity, remediation and quantitative evidence. alternativeSelection.assessment: Two related programmes pass. Closest now integrates the UrbanPlanning/Mobility interest cluster materially through spatial/geospatial/infrastructure study with economics,governance,finance,behaviour and empirical inquiry. SustainableEnergy supplies a distinct second direction. The old rejection of urban study is corrected; it is covered by the closest programme rather than manufactured as a third overlapping variant. All20eligible interests have explicit owners. Full urban/transport/energy engineering and required capstone limitations remain visible.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Partial correspondence through actual sustainability institutions, public/private actors, policy feasibility, stakeholder interests and collective decision-making.
Partial physical foundation through chemical/thermodynamic/mechanical principles, dynamic models and material experiments; UCR does not reproduce the full engineering-physics course.
Shared global environmental and social sustainability concerns; UCR centres climate science, impacts and mitigation rather than the full global-development component.
Life-cycle and circular-economy projects evaluate material/product impacts and resource use; related assessment methods, not the entire industrial-ecology framework.

Advisor-supported sustainability research is a partial project correspondence. UCR topic and techniques vary; this early research course does not reproduce the target’s advanced socio-technical integration project.
Partial spatial-method correspondence through spatial engineering, GIS and remote sensing projects. UCR does not establish the full urban land-use, transport or planning formation.
Financial statements, budgeting and discounted-cash-flow investment appraisal provide related project-finance methods; the urban development and planning context is not reproduced.
Market, firm, consumer and strategic foundations support introductory innovation economics; dedicated innovation content remains a difference.
Public Economics examines externalities, market failure, public goods and policy intervention; a meaningful economic-policy correspondence.
Strategy, digital value and responsible transformation support technology-management inquiry; UCR is not the full dedicated sustainable-technology course.
Actual research design, instruments, empirical collection and statistical analysis support research methodology; the full IE&IS methods framework is broader.
Calculus, differential equations and dynamic modelling provide quantitative foundations.
Probability, estimation, inference and sampling simulation supply mathematical statistical foundations; UCR does not reproduce the complete applied Sustainable Innovation statistics course.
No single selected UCR course establishes this complete required component.
UCR distributes global sustainability and innovation perspectives across courses; no single selected course establishes this full component.
UCR geospatial methods and water/infrastructure perspectives contribute, but do not establish the complete urban-systems modelling course.
Ethical and justice questions occur across UCR courses; no single selected course reproduces this engineering-ethics unit.
Economic, statistical and project methods contribute to assessment, but no selected course reproduces the full dedicated decision-support assessment unit.
UCR business, policy and communication projects support applied innovation, but are not the full dedicated sustainable-technology challenge.
Econometrics supplies causal empirical analysis, and financial appraisal contributes valuation tools; neither is dedicated social cost-benefit analysis.
Global and environmental justice perspectives contribute, but no selected course establishes the full international-development curriculum.
UCR contains real collaborative projects, but no scheduled course establishes the complete multidisciplinary engineering challenge.
Nature-based infrastructure and environmental/spatial projects supply related design practice, but no selected course reproduces the smart-city engineering project.
15 EC of genuine approved open study in year 2 remains open.
Economic and institutional study contributes foundations, but no selected course establishes intellectual-property and competition-law institutions.
TU/e requires an ordinary 10 EC individual final research project. UCR optional independent research is 15 EC outside the scheduled 180 EC.
Technology and society are studied across several courses; no single course establishes this complete engineering-for-society unit.
30 EC of genuine approved open study in year 3 remains open.

notes.text: The UCR options provide related socio-technical sustainability programmes through actual spatial/environmental inquiry, institutions, economic incentives, business, behaviour and research, or through renewable and environmental systems. They do not reproduce TU/e’s full urban/transport engineering, land-use and smart-city design sequence, dedicated IPR/competition-law and social cost-benefit courses, or compulsory final project.

audience.programmeDescription: TU/e Sustainable Innovation studies how technological change interacts with society, institutions, markets and human behaviour. The displayed Urban Planning and Mobility specialization develops spatial and planning analysis of the built environment, transport, facilities and quality of life.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options offer related socio-technical sustainability study through actual economic, institutional, behavioural, spatial and environmental methods. The first incorporates geospatial analysis and nature-based infrastructure; the second emphasizes renewable energy and environmental systems. Both retain gaps in TU/e’s dedicated urban and transport engineering, smart-city project, specialist policy/law methods and compulsory final project.

curriculum.routeLabel: Urban Planning and Mobility specialization; ordinary 10 EC final project
curriculum.limitation: The Sustainable Energy option is a separate evidenced direction within the target programme. The displayed external curriculum remains Urban Planning and Mobility.

componentNotes.si-use-hss: Engineering Ethics and Engineering for Society each carry 5 EC. Personal and professional development is embedded. Five Studium Generale activities and MyFuture activities totaling a value of seven add no credits.
componentNotes.si-multidisciplinary-cbl: Requires completion of previously offered components embedding communication, cooperation, planning and organization skills.
componentNotes.si-year2-open: 15 EC of genuine open study in year 2, followed by 30 EC in year 3. At least 30 EC of the combined 45 EC must be at intermediate or advanced level, including 15 EC at advanced level; content must not overlap. Submit a complete study plan for approval after earning 90 EC.
componentNotes.si-final-project: Required ordinary 10 EC individual research project over year-3 quarters 3 and 4. Entry requires 120 EC, including all compulsory first-year courses, Methodology for IE&IS Research, Assessment to Support Decision Making and either Sustainable Technology in Society: Advanced or Economics of Innovation: Advanced. Preparation begins in the preceding quarter. The optional Innovation Space extension is not added.
componentNotes.si-year3-open: 30 EC of genuine open study. Changes to the approved plan require approval.
